Every number below is a first pass chosen with a simulator (balanceTargets.simulator) from Ctrl C's chapter 3 values, and play decides them. Two entries are NOT importable until engine work exists and John rules on it: the Red Tape event and the Days Off upgrade it unlocks (needsEngineWork).
_meta.usage: The source a typed Assets/Content/chapter-03.json is written from, in the role chapter-02-open-mic.json plays for chapter 2. Two differences from that sheet: conditions, actions, effects and formulas are written in the typed content's own kinds (CurrencyAtLeast, FireGeneratorYield, LinearOnBalance, ...), and every declaration is filed under the scope that declares it (scopes.ch3, scopes.punk_scene, scopes.blues_scene, scopes.metal_scene), so its placement is read off the structure. Ctrl C's original number sits beside each scaled one as `ctrlC`.
_meta.theChapterInOneLine: Three local scenes - punk, blues, metal - each writes its own material and fills its own room; every room pays into one shared pot of Cash, and each scene's farewell show trades that scene's Following for Cred that raises what the scene writes next time.
_meta.shape: Ctrl C's chapter 3 (three divisions feeding a meeting, one prestige per division, a shared upgrade layer, five staged consumption challenges and two others) as a band working three scenes in town. Chapter 2's calendar of gigs gives way to a supply chain: a scene's writing bar and its bought pieces make that genre's Material, and its room turns Material into Cash and Following.
introduces: THREE SCENES as three sibling tiers under the chapter (punk_scene, blues_scene, metal_scene), each with its own Material, Following, pieces, room and prestige. A scene's prestige resets that scene only; the other two keep running and are the head start.

THE ROOM: one per scene, a one-second bar that eats one of its scene's Material per set and pays one Cash and one Following (Ctrl C's Attend Meeting). Supply against consumption is the chapter's balance: a room with no Material stalls, and Material piled up with no room to play it earns nothing.

SHARED CASH ON THE CHAPTER: every room pays the same Cash, Cash buys everything, and every scene's prestige writes Cash to zero (SetCurrency, balance only - the chapter's earned total stands). Cash carries root's `income` tag; Material and Following do not.

CRED PER SCENE (punk_cred, blues_cred, metal_cred, on the chapter): each point raises that scene's Material production by 1% - a payout on what the scene makes, never a bar's fill rate (design 11). The capstone gates on all three.
SCENES OPEN IN ORDER: Punk from the start; Punk's first farewell show sets blues_open; Blues's first sets metal_open.
BIGGER ROOM: a levelled chapter upgrade raising what a room pays AND what it eats (Ctrl C's Larger Meetings) - the supply-versus-consumption decision, made shared.
BOOKING AGENT: one cheap chapter upgrade that makes every room re-book itself (Ctrl C's Schedules). Booked rooms, writing bars, piece bars and passive pieces all earn while away.

DOOR DEAL I-V: five staged events (Ctrl C's Pizza Rules). Stage I's reward is the late twist: rooms stop eating Material, and the Material a scene holds multiplies the Cash its room pays. Each later stage doubles that coefficient.
WRITER'S BLOCK: an event where the writing bars make nothing; the reward is ten times room speed and pay (Ctrl C's Management Styles).
RED TAPE: Ctrl C's Bureaucracy, written in full and marked not importable (needsEngineWork).
_meta.continuityFromCh2: Chapter 2's gig was a bar firing a generator's yield; a room is the same pair (punk_room fires punk_door), and so are a writing bar and its songwriter and each Punk piece and its bar. Chapter 2's standing booking (a chapter flag a bar's repeatWhen reads) is Booking Agent here, one flag for all three rooms. Work the Crowd's taps are Jam here, on the writing and piece bars. Crowd Work's levelled upgrade shape carries Quick Changeovers, Bigger Room, Late-Night Practice and the rest. Battle of the Bands' stages gated on done flags are Door Deal's. What changes: chapter 2 had one tier holding everything; chapter 3 has three sibling tiers, and Cash moves out to the chapter so all three share it.
_meta.deliberatelyNotHere: No fan fatigue: no room carries a perFill, and fatigue waits in design-backlog.md for the touring chapters, 4 and 6. No merch. No rising count of active rooms: one room per scene, always. No CurrencyExceeds counter: Cash is declared on the chapter, so each scene's rung writes it to zero itself and nothing needs a sibling clear.

modelNotes.conditions: Typed kinds with `type`, as Assets/Content writes them: CurrencyAtLeast / EarnedTotalAtLeast (threshold), OwnedCountAtLeast (count), FlagSet (flagId), All / Not, Always.
modelNotes.placement: Lifetime is placement (design 2). The chapter (ch3) holds what all three scenes share and what every scene prestige keeps: Cash, the three Creds, the scene-open and event flags, the shared upgrades, the Cred and twist-free modifiers, the events and the capstone. Each scene tier holds what its own prestige clears: its Material, its Following, its writing bar and songwriter, its room and door, its pieces, its Jam producers, its opening trigger, its twist modifiers and (Punk only) Better Cables and Better Pickups.
modelNotes.scenePair: Every bar here is a bar plus a generator, chapter 2's gig pair: the bar's onComplete is FireGeneratorYield naming the generator, and the generator's yield entries are the payout scaled by its owned count. A writing bar fires its songwriter (Material); a Punk piece bar fires its piece (Material, count = copies bought); a room fires its door (Cash and Following).
modelNotes.openingPurchase: A fired yield is scaled by the generator's owned count, so a writing bar's songwriter and a room's door must be owned to pay. Each is bought once (baseCost 5, availableWhen Not(OwnedCountAtLeast(self, 1)) so the row cannot buy a second copy), and each scene's opening trigger grants the 10 Cash both cost. The trigger is declared in the scene's tier, so every reset of the scene re-arms it and the grant lands after the rung's SetCurrency(cash, 0). Validation refuses a generator baseCost of zero, which is why the grant exists.
modelNotes.room: consumes [{scene material, 1}], fillAmount 1, fillRate 1: one set a second eats one Material. Bigger Room multiplies the door's yield (Cash and Following) and the room's consumption by the same factor, so a room short of Material earns the same and a room with spare Material earns more; Quick Changeovers multiplies the room's fill rate. A room carries no Jam tap: a tap is a payment into the bar's progress, and a paid completion does not drink, so a tapped room would pay Cash and Following for no Material.
modelNotes.cashWipe: Each scene rung writes cash to 0 with SetCurrency. That moves the balance alone: the chapter's earned Cash total stands, so every reveal gated on EarnedTotalAtLeast(cash, ...) stays shown across scene prestiges. The capstone's ResetScope(ch3) is the only thing that clears that total.
modelNotes.credReach: Each Cred modifier (punk_cred_material, ...) is declared on the chapter and listed in the chapter's permanentModifiers. Its effects target the scene's Material currency at `rate` and `yield` - the currency stage, gathered at the Material's home (the scene tier) outward, which meets the chapter. LinearOnBalance computes against that origin, so it reads the scene's Cred by walking out to the chapter. It multiplies Material production (the writing bar's and Punk pieces' fired lumps at yield, the Blues and Metal pieces at rate), never a bar's fill.
modelNotes.twistReach: The twist's Cash factor reads the scene's Material balance, which lives in the scene tier; a modifier on the chapter cannot read it (its formula is validated, and computed, from where it is applied). So each scene declares its own five twist modifiers in its tier and lists them in its own permanentModifiers. Each targets that scene's door at Cash yield (stage 1, gathered from the door's scope, so LinearOnBalance finds the scene's Material) and is switched by appliesWhen on the chapter's Door Deal flags, which an event reward sets. Exactly one stage applies at a time: stage k applies while door_deal_k_done is set and door_deal_(k+1)_done is not.
modelNotes.roomsFree: rooms_free is a chapter modifier with appliesWhen FlagSet(door_deal_1_done): {target: room, currencyId: material, stat: consumption, x0}. Zero is legal on consumption and means free, in the live tick and in the idle claim.
modelNotes.events: All seven events are hosted on the chapter (design 6.1), one at a time. onEntry is RestartScope of each scene (each banks Cred through its own rung's gate, then clears the scene - verified in GameAction.RestartScope: the reach is the acting scope or a scope it encloses, and the scene tiers are enclosed by ch3), then SetCurrency(cash, 0). Cred, the shared upgrades and the flags are on the chapter and survive the entry. The opening triggers re-arm with the resets and grant their 10 Cash at the sweep after the list. onEnd is empty: the attempt is an ordinary run of the three scenes under a handicap, and it simply continues after dismissal. Rewards are lateral, never Cred.
modelNotes.jam: One producer per writing bar and per Punk piece bar, named by the bar's `tap`, paying one second of progress (fillRate 1). They carry the `jam` tag, which Guest List multiplies.
modelNotes.groups: One group per scene listing its bars; maxActive equals the bar count, so every bar runs at once, as Ctrl C runs every division bar. Writing and piece bars repeat always; a room repeats once Booking Agent is bought.
modelNotes.tags: Declared on the chapter: material (the three Material currencies), room (the three room bars), door (the three door generators), writing (the three writing bars), songwriter (the three songwriter generators), piece (every piece generator and every Punk piece bar), jam (the Jam producers). The doors also carry root's `production`, so the Roadie active boost reaches their Cash line; their Following line is not income and the boost's currencyId narrowing keeps it out.

chapter.name: Local Venues
chapter.theme: The club on Third books three nights a week and three different crowds. You play them all: loud and fast in the basement, slow and sad at the juke joint, heavy in the warehouse by the tracks. Each crowd wants new material, and each one you win over makes the next set easier to write.

constants.priceScaleNote: Every Ctrl C Career Capital amount - each price, each event goal - is multiplied by 0.001 here, and the original sits beside it as `ctrlC`. Simulated at 1x, a first clear takes well over ten hours: the room is the only Cash source and pays one per second at the start, so Ctrl C's first Faster Meetings level (4,045) alone is an hour away. At 0.001 the relative prices are Ctrl C's and the opening minutes move. Cycles, yields and multipliers are Ctrl C's unscaled.
constants.generatorCostGrowthNote: Ctrl C's rate for chapters 1-3, on every piece.
constants.credPerPointNote: Ctrl C's +1% per Boost point, as LinearOnBalance(scene_cred, 0.01) on the scene's Material.
constants.scenePrestigeNote: Cred = floor((Following earned this round / divisor) ^ 0.5). The gate is set so the first press pays 5 to 10 Cred; each later press pays four times the Following for twice the Cred. Ctrl C's divisions scale their divisors apart (exp(-11.8), exp(-15.8), exp(-24.8)); here Metal's is the smallest, because before the twist Metal has only its writing bar (its pieces start at 1.1e19 Cash) and must still reach its capstone gate without any event.
constants.doorDealOpensNote: Door Deal I opens once Metal is open and the chapter has earned 1e10 Cash. Its own goal (8.67e6 Cash) is quick by then; this gate is what places the twist late. Once rooms stop eating, every room plays at full speed whatever Material it holds, so Following and Cred jump within minutes (balanceTargets.twistNote).

ch3.flagsNote: blues_open and metal_open are set by the Punk and Blues rungs and read by the Blues and Metal sections, opening triggers and the events. rooms_booked is Booking Agent's switch, read by every room's repeatWhen. The *_release_revealed flags keep each farewell show's card on screen once its gate was first met (a scene tier trigger sets them), since Following is a scene balance that the prestige clears. The done flags retire each event (completedWhen) and switch the twist modifiers and Days Off.

rung.label: Headline the Ballroom
rung.info: The night the three scenes come to one show. Play it and you walk away with another Roadie who stays with the band for good.
rung.confirmText: The town starts over from nothing: every Cred, the Cash, all three scenes and every upgrade go, and only the Roadie comes with you.
rung.note: The capstone (design 6): gates on all three Creds, pays one Roadie, sets the root completion flag, resets the whole chapter. The three gates are the primary pacing knob.

storyBeats.text: The woman from the club on Third books punk on Mondays, blues on Thursdays and metal when nobody else will take the room. She says the trick is to have something new every week. The basement has a PA, a drain in the floor and thirty kids who want it loud. Write fast.

The punks, the blues regulars and the metal kids have never been in one room before. Tonight it is the ballroom, your name at the top of the bill, and all three crowds sing the same chorus back at you. Someone from a booking agency two states over leaves a card on the monitor. Dave says the van will make it. Probably.

sectionsNote: Every region gates on a flag or on the chapter's earned Cash total, never a spendable balance (design 2). The chapter's earned Cash survives scene prestiges (SetCurrency moves the balance only), so a row shown once stays shown until the capstone. The farewell-show cards gate on chapter flags because Following is a scene balance the prestige clears.

balanceTargets.simulator: C:/Users/jsp73/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/bfcb6f51b40d725f/a5c44597-f301-4be2-b0f6-f18880a62607/scratchpad/ch3sim.py (scratch, not kept in the repo). Active play at one-second steps; no taps, no Encore, no Roadies, no idle. The player buys whatever repays soonest (time to afford plus time to repay), saves for it when it is not affordable, presses a farewell show when it pays at least twice the Cred banked (the first press of each scene at once), and enters an event when a trial run shows its goal reachable within 20 minutes.

simulatedFirstClear.withDoorDealI: Punk farewell 9 min (Blues opens), Blues farewell 52 min (Metal opens), Metal farewell 64 min, Door Deal I opens and clears 130-131 min, capstone armed 132 min. Farewell shows: Punk 6, Blues 4, Metal 7.
simulatedFirstClear.withNoEvent: Same to 110 min, then the pre-twist plateau: capstone armed 287 min. Farewell shows: Punk 5, Blues 4, Metal 4 - thirteen, chapter 2's 10-14.
simulatedFirstClear.pressRule: Pressing at the first doubling instead: 152 min with Door Deal I, 230 min without. At a tripling: 132 and 297.

balanceTargets.targetClear: About 2 h 10 min with Door Deal I, about 4 h 45 min with no event: past chapter 2's 1.5-2 h, as a three-scene chapter should be, and completable without any event (design 6.1).
balanceTargets.twistNote: Door Deal I ends the chapter's pacing: with rooms no longer eating, every room plays at the full speed the shared upgrades allow whatever Material it holds, so Following - and through it Cred - stops depending on the scene's own supply, and the twist's Cash buys out Quick Changeovers and Bigger Room within minutes. The capstone arms within two minutes of the twist. Play past it reaches what the first clear does not: in the simulator Door Deal II and III, Writer's Block, Tight Arrangements, every Metal piece and Songwriting Retreat all land within 50 minutes of the twist. Under Ctrl C the same reward frees the meeting but its prestige reads Progress, so its prestige still depends on supply; here it reads Following.
balanceTargets.notReachedBeforeTheCapstone: Late-Night Practice 7-9, Quick Changeovers 16-19, Bigger Room 17, Home Studio 2-7, Better Cables 4-6, Better Pickups, Tight Arrangements, Songwriting Retreat, every Metal piece, Door Deal II-V, Writer's Block (all reachable after the twist, before the player chooses to press the capstone).
balanceTargets.primaryPacingKnob: the three capstone gates (400 / 100 / 50 Cred) - raise or lower before touching a curve
secondaryKnobs: priceScale (0.001) - the whole Cash ladder against a room's one Cash a set.
doorDealOpensAtCashEarned (1e10) - where the twist lands, and therefore where the evented clear ends.
each scene's gate and divisor - when a scene's first farewell show comes and how fast its Cred doubles.
the opening price (5) and grant (10) - only that the first purchases are affordable.
watchList: If the plateau before the twist (about 110 to 280 min without events) feels like a wall, lower the capstone gates or move Door Deal I earlier before touching prices.
If Metal's farewell shows feel pointless before the twist (Metal writes from its writing bar alone until 1.1e19 Cash), lower Metal's gate rather than its piece prices.
Tapping is not simulated: Jam on the writing and piece bars speeds the opening minutes, never a room.
balanceTargets.tuneAgainst: a player with Encore up to 4x and Roadies stationed from chapters 1 and 2; confirm the plateau still takes play time and that Door Deal I is beatable unbuffed when it opens.
